field.name: CFG_BOD_VBAT_RESET_ENABLED
field.description: When BOD VDDMAIN analog detector is turned on and BOD VDDMAIN reset is enabled, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_BOD_CORE_RESET_ENABLED
field.description: When BOD CORE analog detector is turned on and BOD CORE reset is enabled, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_BOD_VBAT_IRQ_ENABLED
field.description: When BOD VDDMAIN analog detector is turned on and BOD VDDMAIN IRQ is enabled, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_WDT_ENABLED
field.description: When WatchDog Timer is activated, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_CWDT_ENABLED
field.description: When Code WatchDog Timer is activated, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_ELS_GDET_ENABLED
field.description: When ELS GDET is enabled, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_TAMPER_DET_ENABLED
field.description: When tamper detector is enabled in RTC, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_FLASH_IS_REMAPPED
field.description: When FLASHREMAP_OFFSET register (0x4000_0448) is not equal to 0x0000_0000, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_FLASH_IS_REMAPPED_DP
field.description: When FLASHREMAP_OFFSET_DP register (0x4000_044C) is not equal to 0x0000_0000, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_FLASH_BANK0_ENABLE
field.description: The state of FLASHBANK_ENABLE0 register (0x4000_0450) reflects to this register as below.

field.name: CFG_FLASH_BANK1_ENABLE
field.description: The state of FLASHBANK_ENABLE1 register (0x4000_0454) reflects to this register as below:

field.name: CFG_QK_DISABLE_ENROLL
field.description: When CONFIG[DIS_PUF_ENROLL] bit is set 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_QK_DISABLE_WRAP
field.description: When CONFIG[DIS_PUF_WRAP_KEY] bit is set 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_DIS_STRICT_MODE
field.description: When "CFG_SEC_ENA_SEC_CHK" indicates state 0 or when "DISABLE_STRICT_MODE" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are equal to 01, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_DIS_VIOL_ABORT
field.description: When "DISABLE_VIOLATION_ABORT" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_ENA_NS_PRIV_CHK
field.description: When "ENABLE_NS_PRIV_CHECK" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_ENA_S_PRIV_CHK
field.description: When "ENABLE_S_PRIV_CHECK" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_ENA_SEC_CHK
field.description: When "ENABLE_SECURE_CHECKING" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_IDAU_ALLNS
field.description: When "IDAU_ALL_NS" bits in "MISC_CTRL_REG" and "MISC_CTRL_DP_REG" on AHB secure controller, both bits are equal to 01, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_LOCK_NS_MPU
field.description: When "LOCK_NS_MPU" bits in "CPU0_LOCK_REG" on AHB secure controller are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_LOCK_NS_VTOR
field.description: When "LOCK_NS_VTOR" bits in "CPU0_LOCK_REG" on AHB secure controller are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_LOCK_S_MPU
field.description: When "LOCK_S_MPU" bits in "CPU0_LOCK_REG" on AHB secure controller are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_LOCK_S_VTAIRCR
field.description: When "LOCK_S_VTAIRCR" bits in "CPU0_LOCK_REG" on AHB secure controller are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: CFG_SEC_LOCK_SAU
field.description: When "LOCK_SAU" bits in "CPU0_LOCK_REG" on AHB secure controller are not equal to 10, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_CPU0_DBGEN
field.description: When CPU0 (CM33) "deben" input is state 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_CPU0_NIDEN
field.description: When CPU0 (CM33) "niden" input is state 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_CPU0_SPIDEN
field.description: When CPU0 (CM33) "spiden" input is state 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_CPU0_SPNIDEN
field.description: When CPU0 (CM33) "spniden" input is state 1, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_DAP_ENABLE_CPU0
field.description: When DAP to AP0 for CPU0 (CM33) debug access is allowed, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_ELS_DEBUG_EN
field.description: When ELS uCode code fetch out of AHB for debug is enabled, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_ALLOW_TEST_ACCESS
field.description: When JTAG TAP access is allowed, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_XO32K_FAILED
field.description: When XO32K oscillation fail flag is state 1 in PMC register block, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_QK_PUF_SCORE
field.description: These register bits indicate the state of "qk_puf_score[3:0]" outputs from QK PUF block.

field.name: ST_QK_ZEROIZED
field.description: This register bit indicates the state of "qk_zeroized" output from QK PUF block.

field.name: ST_MAIN_CLK_IS_EXT
field.description: When MAIN_CLK is running from external clock source either XO32M, XO32K or GPIO CLKIN, this bit indicates state 1.

field.name: ST_DCDC_VOUT
field.description: VOUT[3:0] setting on DCDC0 register in PMC block will reflect to this register.

field.name: ST_BOOT_MODE
field.description: BOOTMODE[1:0] status on STATUS register in PMC block will reflect to this register.

field.name: FLAG_AP_ENABLE_CPU0
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when DAP enables AP0 for CPU0 (CM33) debug access. The register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_BOD_VBAT_RESET_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when BOD VDDMAIN reset is enabled and BOD VDDMAIN analog detector is tripped. This register is cleared 0 by AO domain POR.

field.name: FLAG_BOD_CORE_RESET_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when BOD CORE reset is enabled and BOD CORE analog detector is tripped. This register is cleared 0 by AO domain POR.

field.name: FLAG_BOD_VBAT_IRQ_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when BOD VDDMAIN IRQ is enabled and BOD VDDMAIN analog detector is tripped. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_BOD_CORE_IRQ_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when BOD CORE IRQ is enabled and BOD CORE analog detector is tripped. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_WDT_RESET_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when WatchDog Timer reset is enabled and reset event is triggered. This register is cleared 0 by AO domain POR.

field.name: FLAG_CWDT_RESET_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when Code WatchDog Timer reset is enabled and reset event is triggered. This register is cleared 0 by AO domain POR.

field.name: FLAG_WDT_IRQ_OCCURED
field.description: This flag register is set 1 when WatchDog Timer IRQ is enabled and IRQ event is triggered. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_CWDT_IRQ_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when Code WatchDog Timer IRQ is enabled and IRQ event is triggered. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_QK_ERROR
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when QK_ERROR is flagged from QK PUF block. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_ELS_GLITCH_DETECTED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when GDET error is flagged from ELS. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_TAMPER_EVENT_DETECTED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when tamper event is flagged from RTC. This register is cleared 0 by AO domain POR or by PMC reset event, if ranmpr detection event is cleared by software.

field.name: FLAG_FLASH_ECC_INVALID
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when FLASH controller indicates ECC error. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_SEC_VIOL_IRQ_OCURRED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when security violation is indicated from FLASH sub-system or AHB bus matrix.

field.name: FLAG_CPU0_NS_C_ACC_OCCURED
field.description: This flag bit is set 1 when CPU0 (CM33) makes non-secure code transactions. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

field.name: FLAG_CPU0_NS_D_ACC_OCCURED
field.description: This flag register is set 1 when CPU0 (CM33) makes non-secure data transactions. This register is cleared 0 by PMC reset event.

register.name: IENR
register.description: Pin Interrupt Level or Rising Edge Interrupt Enable

enumeratedValue.name: ENRL_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disable rising edge or level interrupt

enumeratedValue.name: ENRL_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable rising edge or level interrupt

register.name: SIENR
register.description: Pin Interrupt Level or Rising Edge Interrupt Set

enumeratedValue.name: SETENRL_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable rising edge or level interrupt

register.name: CIENR
register.description: Pin Interrupt Level (Rising Edge Interrupt) Clear

enumeratedValue.name: CENRL_1
enumeratedValue.description: Disable rising edge or level interrupt

register.name: IENF
register.description: Pin Interrupt Active Level or Falling Edge Interrupt Enable

enumeratedValue.name: ENAF_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disable falling edge interrupt or set active interrupt level LOW

enumeratedValue.name: ENAF_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable falling edge interrupt enabled or set active interrupt level HIGH

register.name: SIENF
register.description: Pin Interrupt Active Level or Falling Edge Interrupt Set

enumeratedValue.name: SETENAF_1
enumeratedValue.description: Select HIGH-active interrupt or enable falling edge interrupt

register.name: CIENF
register.description: Pin Interrupt Active Level or Falling Edge Interrupt Clear

enumeratedValue.name: CENAF_1
enumeratedValue.description: LOW-active interrupt selected or falling edge interrupt disabled

enumeratedValue.name: RDET_0
enumeratedValue.description: Read 0- No rising edge has been detected on this pin since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit, Write 0- no operation

enumeratedValue.name: RDET_1
enumeratedValue.description: Read 1- a rising edge has been detected since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit, Write 1- clear rising edge detection for this pin

enumeratedValue.name: FDET_0
enumeratedValue.description: Read 0- No falling edge has been detected on this pin since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit, Write 0- no operation

enumeratedValue.name: FDET_1
enumeratedValue.description: Read 1- a falling edge has been detected since Reset or the last time a one was written to this bit, Write 1- clear falling edge detection for this bit

enumeratedValue.name: PSTAT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Read 0- interrupt is not being requested for this pin, Write 0- no operation.

enumeratedValue.name: PSTAT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Read 1- interrupt is being requested for this pin, Write 1 (edge-sensitive)- clear rising- and falling-edge detection for this pin, Write 1 (level-sensitive)- switch the active level for this pin (in the IENF register).

field.name: SEL_PMATCH
field.description: Specifies whether the pin interrupts are controlled by the pin interrupt function or by the pattern match function.

enumeratedValue.name: PIN_INTERRUPT
enumeratedValue.description: Pin interrupt- interrupts are driven in response to the standard pin interrupt function.

enumeratedValue.name: PATTERN_MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: Pattern match- interrupts are driven in response to pattern matches.

register.name: PMCFG
register.description: Pattern Match Interrupt Bit Slice Configuration

field.name: PROD_ENDPTS0
field.description: Determines whether slice 0 is an endpoint.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_EFFECT
enumeratedValue.description: No effect. Slice 0 is not an endpoint.

enumeratedValue.name: ENDPOINT
enumeratedValue.description: Endpoint. Slice 0 is the endpoint of a product term (minterm). Pin interrupt 0 in the NVIC is raised if the minterm evaluates as true.

field.name: CFG0
field.description: Specifies the match contribution condition for bit slice 0.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising edge. Match occurs if a rising edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky falling edge. Match occurs if a falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs if either a rising or falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: HIGH_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: High level. Match (for this bit slice) occurs when there is a high level on the input specified for this bit slice in the PMSRC register.

enumeratedValue.name: LOW_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: Low level. Match occurs when there is a low level on the specified input.

enumeratedValue.name: CONSTANT_ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Constant 0. This bit slice never contributes to a match (should be used to disable any unused bit slices).

enumeratedValue.name: EVENT
enumeratedValue.description: Event. Non-sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs on an event when either a rising or falling edge is first detected on the specified input (this is a non-sticky version of value 0x3). This bit is cleared after 1 clock cycle.

field.name: CFG1
field.description: Specifies the match contribution condition for bit slice 1.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising edge. Match occurs if a rising edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky falling edge. Match occurs if a falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: STICKY_RISING_FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs if either a rising or falling edge on the specified input has occurred since the last time the edge detection for this bit slice was cleared. This match condition is only cleared when the PMCFG or the PMSRC registers are written to.

enumeratedValue.name: HIGH_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: High level. Match (for this bit slice) occurs when there is a high level on the input specified for this bit slice in the PMSRC register.

enumeratedValue.name: LOW_LEVEL
enumeratedValue.description: Low level. Match occurs when there is a low level on the specified input.

enumeratedValue.name: CONSTANT_ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Constant 0. This bit slice never contributes to a match (should be used to disable any unused bit slices).

enumeratedValue.name: EVENT
enumeratedValue.description: Event. Non-sticky rising or falling edge. Match occurs on an event when either a rising or falling edge is first detected on the specified input (this is a non-sticky version of value 0x3). This bit is cleared after 1 clock cycle.

field.name: RESULT
field.description: Indicates the measurement result-either the target clock counter value (for Frequency Measurement mode) or pulse width measurement (for Pulse Width Measurement mode)

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Timeout disabled, if timeout is configured

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disable open-drain stop. ODSTOP must be disabled when sending an HDR exit pattern.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable open-drain stop. STOP is emitted at open-drain speeds even for I3C messages. In legacy devices, this feature can ensure that the legacy devices see the STOP.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: ODHPP disabled. Open-Drain SCL High half-clock period is the same as the Open-Drain Low SCL half-period.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: ODHPP enabled. Open-Drain High SCL half-lock period is one PPBAUD count for I3C messages. This setting is faster (and works for I3C devices). Any legacy I2C devices on the bus will not see the SCL High at all (less than the spike filter period).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Target ignores the I2C or I3C bus

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Target can operate on the I2C or I3C bus

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Always NACK enable. The target rejects all requests to it, except for a Common Command Code (CCC) broadcast. NACK = 1 should be used with caution, because the controller may decide that the target is missing, if NACK is overused.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Match START or STOP enable. START and STOP sticky SSTATUS bits only become 1 when SSTATUS[MATCHED] is 1. This setting allows START and STOP to be used to detect the end of a message to/from this target.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Ignore TE0/TE1 errors. Target does not detect TE0 or TE1 errors, so it does not lock up waiting on an Exit Pattern. This setting should only be used when the bus does not use HDR mode.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: SIDPARTNO[PARTNO] is a part number and an instance.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enables wait to ensure the bus is not in HDR mode.

enumeratedValue.name: STOPPED
enumeratedValue.description: I3C module is in a STOP condition.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: Bus target not listening or responding.

enumeratedValue.name: BUSY
enumeratedValue.description: This bus target is listening to the bus traffic or responding.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: No CCC message is being handled.

enumeratedValue.name: BUSY
enumeratedValue.description: A CCC message is being handled automatically.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: REQ in process is not an SDR read from this target.

enumeratedValue.name: BUSY
enumeratedValue.description: The REQ in process is an SDR read from this target, or an In-Band Interrupt (IBI) is being pushed out.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: REQ in process is not SDR write data from the controller.

enumeratedValue.name: BUSY
enumeratedValue.description: REQ in process is SDR write data from the controller to this bus target (or all I3C targets), but not in ENTDAA mode.

enumeratedValue.name: IN_ENTDAA
enumeratedValue.description: I3C bus is in Enter Dynamic Address Assignment (ENTDAA) mode, regardless of whether this bus target has a Dynamic Address or not.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_IN_HDR_DDR
enumeratedValue.description: I3C bus not in HDR-DDR mode

enumeratedValue.name: IN_HDR_DDR
enumeratedValue.description: The I3C bus is in HDR-DDR mode , regardless of whether HDR mode is supported by this module or not, and regardless of whether the message is to this module or to some other module.

enumeratedValue.name: START_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: A START or repeated START was seen after the START bit was last cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCHED
enumeratedValue.description: An incoming header matched the I3C Dynamic or I2C Static address of this device (if any) since the bus was last cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: STOP_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Stopped state detected. A STOP state was present on the bus since the bus was last cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: CHANGE_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: DA change detected. The target DA has been assigned, re-assigned, or reset (lost) and is now in the state of being valid or none.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCH
enumeratedValue.description: HDR command matched the I3C Dynamic Address of this device.

enumeratedValue.name: EVENT
enumeratedValue.description: An IBI, CR, or HJ has occurred.

field.description: The last chip reset was caused by a System Reset requested by the ARM CPU.

field.name: WDTRESET
field.description: The last chip reset was caused by the Watchdog Timer.

field.name: SWRRESET
field.description: The last chip reset was caused by a Software event.

field.name: DPDRESET_WAKEUPIO

field.name: DPDRESET_RTC
field.description: A RTC event occured during DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode.

field.name: DPDRESET_OSTIMER
field.description: An OS Timer event occured during a DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode.

field.name: CDOGRESET
field.description: The last chip reset was caused by the code Watchdog.

field.name: DPD_EVENTS_ORDER
field.description: In DEEP-POWER-DOWN mode, indicates which reset event occured first, between a wake up I/O event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN), a RTC event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN) and a OS Timer event (in DEEP-POWER-DOWN). May be usefull when several reset events are enabled during DEEP-POWER-DOWN.

enumeratedValue.name: WAKEUPIO_RTC

enumeratedValue.name: WAKEUPIO_OSTIMER

enumeratedValue.name: RTC_OSTIMER

enumeratedValue.name: WAKEUPIO_RTC_OSTIMER

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Hardware triggering not used for channel.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

enumeratedValue.name: EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED

field.name: VALIDPENDING

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_TRIGGERED

enumeratedValue.name: TRIGGERED

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED

enumeratedValue.name: DUAL_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Dual counter. The SCT operates as two 16-bit counters named COUNTER_L and COUNTER_H.

enumeratedValue.name: UNIFIED_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Unified counter. The SCT operates as a unified 32-bit counter.

enumeratedValue.name: SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the entire SCT module including all counters and counter prescalers.

enumeratedValue.name: SAMPLED_SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Sampled System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the SCT module, but the counter and prescalers are only enabled to count when the designated edge is detected on the input selected by the CKSEL field. The minimum pulse width on the selected clock-gate input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the high-performance, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SCT_INPUT_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: SCT Input Clock Mode. The input/edge selected by the CKSEL field clocks the SCT module, including all counters and prescalers, after first being synchronized to the system clock. The minimum pulse width on the clock input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the low-power, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ASYNCHRONOUS_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Asynchronous Mode. The entire SCT module is clocked directly by the input/edge selected by the CKSEL field. In this mode, the SCT outputs are switched synchronously to the SCT input clock - not the system clock. The input clock rate must be at least half the system clock rate and can be the same or faster than the system clock.

field.name: CKSEL
field.description: SCT Clock Select. The specific functionality of the designated input/edge is dependent on the CLKMODE bit selection in this register.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RELOAD
enumeratedValue.description: No Reload. Prevents the lower match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RELOAD_H
enumeratedValue.description: No Reload. Prevents the higher match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The L or unified counter is counting up.

enumeratedValue.name: DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Down. The L or unified counter is counting down.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The counter counts up to a limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Up-down. The counter counts up to a limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The H counter is counting up.

enumeratedValue.name: DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Down. The H counter is counting down.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The H counter counts up to its limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Up-down. The H counter counts up to its limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

field.name: STARTMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_L] = 0 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STARTMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_H] = 0 (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: DITHER_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_L] = 0 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: DITHER_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_H] = 0 (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: ID
field.description: Module identifier for the selected function

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The I2C Master function is disabled. When disabled, the Master configuration settings are not changed, but the Master function is internally reset.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The I2C Master function is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The I2C slave function is disabled. When disabled, the Slave configuration settings are not changed, but the Slave function is internally reset.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The I2C slave function is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The I2C Monitor function is disabled. When disabled, the Monitor function configuration settings are not changed, but the Monitor function is internally reset.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The I2C Monitor function is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The time-out function is disabled. When disabled, the time-out function is internally reset.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The time-out function is enabled. Both types of time-out flags will be generated and will cause interrupts if those flags are enabled. Typically, only one time-out flag will be used in a system.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The Monitor function will not perform clock stretching. Software or DMA may not always be able to read data provided by the Monitor function before it (the data) is overwritten. This mode can be used when non-invasive monitoring is critical.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The Monitor function will perform clock stretching, to ensure that the software or DMA can read all incoming data supplied by the Monitor function.

enumeratedValue.name: IN_PROGRESS
enumeratedValue.description: In progress. Communication is in progress and the Master function is busy and cannot currently accept a command.

enumeratedValue.name: PENDING
enumeratedValue.description: Pending. The Master function needs software service or is in the idle state. If the master is not in the idle state, then the master is waiting to receive or transmit data, or is waiting for the NACK bit.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: Idle. The Master function is available to be used for a new transaction.

enumeratedValue.name: RECEIVE_READY
enumeratedValue.description: Receive ready. Received data is available (in Master Receiver mode). Address plus Read was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.

enumeratedValue.name: TRANSMIT_READY
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit ready. Data can be transmitted (in Master Transmitter mode). Address plus Write was previously sent and Acknowledged by a slave.

enumeratedValue.name: NACK_DATA
enumeratedValue.description: NACK Data. Slave NACKed transmitted data.

enumeratedValue.name: ARBITRATION_LOSS
enumeratedValue.description: Arbitration loss. The Master function has experienced an Arbitration Loss. At this point, the Master function has already stopped driving the bus and has gone into an idle state. Software can respond by doing nothing, or by sending a Start (to attempt to gain control of the bus when the bus next becomes idle).

enumeratedValue.name: ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: The Master function has experienced a Start/Stop Error. A Start or Stop was detected at a time when Start or Stop is not allowed by the I2C specification. The Master interface has stopped driving the bus and gone into an idle state; no action is required. A request for a Start could be made, or software could attempt to make sure that the bus has not stalled.

enumeratedValue.name: IN_PROGRESS
enumeratedValue.description: In progress. The Slave function does not currently need software service.

enumeratedValue.name: PENDING
enumeratedValue.description: Pending. The Slave function needs software service. Information about what is needed is in the Slave state field (SLVSTATE).

enumeratedValue.name: SLAVE_ADDRESS
enumeratedValue.description: Slave address. Address plus R/W received. At least one of the 4 slave addresses has been matched by hardware.

enumeratedValue.name: SLAVE_RECEIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Slave receive. Received data is available (in Slave Receiver mode).

enumeratedValue.name: SLAVE_TRANSMIT
enumeratedValue.description: Slave transmit. Data can be transmitted (in Slave Transmitter mode).

enumeratedValue.name: STRETCHING
enumeratedValue.description: Stretching. The slave function is currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-Sleepmode cannot be entered at this time.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_STRETCHING
enumeratedValue.description: Not stretching. The slave function is not currently stretching the I2C bus clock. Deep-sleep mode can be entered at this time.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_SELECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Not selected. The Slave function is not currently selected.

enumeratedValue.name: SELECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Selected. The Slave function is currently selected.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_DESELECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Not deselected. The Slave function has not become deselected. This does not mean that the Slave is currently selected. That information is in the SLVSEL flag.

enumeratedValue.name: DESELECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Deselected. The Slave function has become deselected. This is specifically caused by the SLVSEL flag changing from 1 to 0. See SLVSEL for details about when that event occurs.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_DATA
enumeratedValue.description: No data. The Monitor function does not currently have data available.

enumeratedValue.name: DATA_WAITING
enumeratedValue.description: Data waiting. The Monitor function has data waiting to be read.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_OVERRUN
enumeratedValue.description: No overrun. Monitor data has not overrun.

enumeratedValue.name: OVERRUN
enumeratedValue.description: Overrun. A Monitor data overrun has occurred. An overrun can only happen when Monitor clock stretching not enabled via the CFG[MONCLKSTR] bit. Writing 1 to MONOV bit clears the MONOV flag.

enumeratedValue.name: INACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Inactive. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be inactive.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Active. The Monitor function considers the I2C bus to be active.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: Not idle. The I2C bus is not idle, or MONIDLE flag has been cleared by software.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: Idle. The I2C bus has gone idle at least once, since the last time MONIDLE flag was cleared by software.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: No time-out. I2C bus events have not caused a time-out.

enumeratedValue.name: EVEN_TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: Event time-out. The time between I2C bus events has been longer than the time specified by the TIMEOUT register.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: No time-out. SCL low time has not caused a time-out.

enumeratedValue.name: TIMEOUT
enumeratedValue.description: Time-out. SCL low time has caused a time-out.

enumeratedValue.name: CONTINUE
enumeratedValue.description: Continue. Informs the Master function to continue to the next operation. This action must done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation.

enumeratedValue.name: START
enumeratedValue.description: Start. A Start will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time.

enumeratedValue.name: STOP
enumeratedValue.description: Stop. A Stop will be generated on the I2C bus at the next allowed time, preceded by a NACK to the slave if the master is receiving data from the slave (in Master Receiver mode).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disable. No DMA requests are generated for master operation.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A DMA request is generated for I2C master data operations. When this I2C master is generating Acknowledge bits in Master Receiver mode, the acknowledge is generated automatically.

enumeratedValue.name: CONTINUE
enumeratedValue.description: Continue. Informs the Slave function to continue to the next operation, by clearing the STAT[SLVPENDING] flag. This must be done after writing transmit data, reading received data, or any other housekeeping related to the next bus operation. Automatic Operation has different requirements. SLVCONTINUE should not be set unless SLVPENDING = 1.

enumeratedValue.name: NACK
enumeratedValue.description: NACK. Causes the Slave function to NACK the master when the slave is receiving data from the master (in Slave Receiver mode).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. No DMA requests are issued for Slave mode operation.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. DMA requests are issued for I2C slave data transmission and reception.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal, non-automatic operation. If AUTONACK = 0, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated when a matching address is received. If AUTONACK = 1, then received addresses are NACKed (ignored).

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOMATIC_ACK
enumeratedValue.description: A header with matching SLVADR0 and matching direction as set by AUTOMATCHREAD will be ACKed immediately, allowing the master to move on to the data bytes. If the address matches SLVADR0, but the direction does not match AUTOMATCHREAD, then the behavior will depend on the SLVADR0[AUTONACK] bit: if AUTONACK is set, then it will be Nacked; if AUTONACK is clear, then a SlvPending interrupt is generated.

enumeratedValue.name: I2C_WRITE
enumeratedValue.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C write.

enumeratedValue.name: I2C_READ
enumeratedValue.description: In Automatic Mode, the expected next operation is an I2C read.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOMATIC
enumeratedValue.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. Slave Address n is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Ignored. Slave Address n is ignored.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal operation, matching I2C addresses are not ignored.

enumeratedValue.description: Automatic-only mode. All incoming addresses are ignored (NACKed), unless AUTOACK is set, and the address matches SLVADRn, and AUTOMATCHREAD matches the direction.

enumeratedValue.name: MASK
enumeratedValue.description: Mask. The SLVQUAL0 field is used as a logical mask for matching address 0.

enumeratedValue.name: EXTEND
enumeratedValue.description: Extend. The SLVQUAL0 field is used to extend address 0 matching in a range of addresses.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_START_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: No start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Start event on the I2C bus.

enumeratedValue.name: START_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Start event on the I2C bus.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: No repeated start detected. The Monitor function has not detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.

enumeratedValue.name: DETECTED
enumeratedValue.description: Repeated start detected. The Monitor function has detected a Repeated Start event on the I2C bus.

enumeratedValue.name: ACKNOWLEDGED
enumeratedValue.description: Acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was acknowledged by at least one master or slave receiver.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED
enumeratedValue.description: Not acknowledged. The data currently being provided by the Monitor function was not acknowledged by any receiver.

field.name: EMPTYTX
field.description: Empty command for the transmit FIFO. When a 1 is written to this bit, the TX FIFO is emptied.

field.name: EMPTYRX
field.description: Empty command for the receive FIFO. When a 1 is written to this bit, the RX FIFO is emptied.

enumeratedValue.name: DO_NOT_POP
enumeratedValue.description: Debug reads of the FIFO do not pop the FIFO.

enumeratedValue.name: POP
enumeratedValue.description: A debug read causes the FIFO to pop.

enumeratedValue.name: EMPTY
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit FIFO is empty; however, the peripheral may still be processing the last piece of data.

enumeratedValue.name: FULL
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit FIFO is full, and another write would cause an overflow

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_FULL
enumeratedValue.description: Transmit FIFO is not full, so more data can be written

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_EMPTY

enumeratedValue.description: RX FIFO timeout counter is not reset every time data is transferred from the peripheral into the RX FIFO.

enumeratedValue.description: RX FIFO timeout counter is reset when the RX FIFO becomes empty.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: RX FIFO timeout counter is not reset when the RX FIFO becomes empty.

cluster.name: CHANNEL[%s]
cluster.description: Array of registers: DC_CTRL, DIVHFCLK, FIFO_CTRL, FIFO_DATA, FIFO_STATUS, GAINSHIFT, OSR, PHY_CTRL, PREAC2FSCOEF, PREAC4FSCOEF

enumeratedValue.name: COMP0
enumeratedValue.description: Compensation = 0. This is the recommended setting.

enumeratedValue.name: COMP0
enumeratedValue.description: Compensation = 0. This is the recommended setting.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FIFO is enabled. The FIFO must be enabled in order for the CPU or DMA to read data from the DMIC via the FIFODATA register.

enumeratedValue.name: RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Reset the FIFO. This must be cleared before resuming operation.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: FIFO level interrupts are not enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: DMA requests based on FIFO level are enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ONEENTRY
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger when the FIFO has received one entry (is no longer empty).

enumeratedValue.name: TWOENTRIES
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger when the FIFO has received two entries.

enumeratedValue.name: ENTRIES15
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger when the FIFO has received 15 entries.

enumeratedValue.name: ENTRIES16
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger when the FIFO has received 16 entries (has become full).

field.name: PHY_FALL
field.description: Capture DMIC on Falling edge (0 means on rising)

enumeratedValue.name: RISING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Capture PDM_DATA on the rising edge of PDM_CLK.

enumeratedValue.name: FALLING_EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Capture PDM_DATA on the falling edge of PDM_CLK.

field.name: PHY_HALF
field.description: Use Half rate sampling (ie Clock to dmic is sent at half the speed than the decimator is providing)

enumeratedValue.name: STANDARD
enumeratedValue.description: Standard half rate sampling. The clock to the DMIC is sent at the same rate as the decimator is providing.

enumeratedValue.name: HALF_RATE
enumeratedValue.description: Use half rate sampling. The clock to the DMIC is sent at half the rate that the decimator is providing.

enumeratedValue.name: DO_NOT_SATURATE
enumeratedValue.description: Do not Saturate. Results roll over if out range and do not saturate.

enumeratedValue.name: SATURATE
enumeratedValue.description: Saturate. If the result overflows, it saturates at 0xFFFF for positive overflow and 0x8000 for negative overflow.

enumeratedValue.name: USE_1FS
enumeratedValue.description: Use 1 FS output for PCM data.

enumeratedValue.name: USE_2FS
enumeratedValue.description: Use 2 FS output for PCM data.

field.name: HPFS
field.description: The HPFS field chooses the High Pass filter in first part of HWVAD.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal operation, waiting for HWVAD trigger event (stage 0).

enumeratedValue.name: RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Reset internal interrupt flag by writing a '1' (stage 1) pulse.

field.name: WAS
field.description: Write CRC DATA register As Seed

enumeratedValue.name: WAS_0
enumeratedValue.description: Writes to the CRC DATA register are data values.

enumeratedValue.name: WAS_1
enumeratedValue.description: Writes to the CRC DATA register are seed values.

field.name: FXOR
field.description: Complement Read Of CRC DATA register

enumeratedValue.name: FXOR_1
enumeratedValue.description: Invert or complement the read value of the CRC DATA register.

enumeratedValue.name: TOTR_1
enumeratedValue.description: Bits in bytes are transposed; bytes are not transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: TOTR_2
enumeratedValue.description: Both bits in bytes and bytes are transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: TOTR_3
enumeratedValue.description: Only bytes are transposed; no bits in a byte are transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: TOT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Bits in bytes are transposed; bytes are not transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: TOT_2
enumeratedValue.description: Both bits in bytes and bytes are transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: TOT_3
enumeratedValue.description: Only bytes are transposed; no bits in a byte are transposed.

enumeratedValue.name: OVERRUN_ERR
enumeratedValue.description: Debug overrun error. A debug overrun occurred.

enumeratedValue.name: AHB_OVERRUN_ERR
enumeratedValue.description: AHB Overrun Error. An AHB overrun occurred.

enumeratedValue.name: SAMPLE_POINT
enumeratedValue.description: The sample point can be monitored at the CAN_TXD.

field.name: RX
field.description: Monitors the Actual Value of the CAN_RXD

enumeratedValue.name: NO_WRITE_ACCESS
enumeratedValue.description: No write access. The CPU has no write access to the protected configuration registers.

enumeratedValue.name: WRITE_ACCESS
enumeratedValue.description: Write access. The CPU has write access to the protected configuration registers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: MCAN may be set in Power Down mode by stopping the internal MCAN clocks.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Clock stop requested. When clock stop is requested, first INIT and then CSA will be set after all pending transfer requests have been completed and the CAN bus reaches idle.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Automatic retransmission of messages not transmitted successfully enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Bit rate switching for transmissions is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Bit rate switching for transmission is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Two consecutive dominant quanta required to detect an edge for hard synchronization.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: CAN FD frame format will follow according to ISO11898-1.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: CAN FD frame format will follow according to Bosch CAN FD Specification V1.0.

field.name: NTSEG2
field.description: Nominal Time Segment After Sample Point

field.name: NTSEG1
field.description: Nominal Time Segment Before Sample Point

enumeratedValue.name: TCP_BITS
enumeratedValue.description: Timestamp counter value incremented according to TCP bits

enumeratedValue.name: TX_EVNT_FIFO
enumeratedValue.description: Timeout is controlled by Tx event FIFO.

enumeratedValue.name: RX_FIFO_0
enumeratedValue.description: Timeout is controlled by Rx FIFO 0.

enumeratedValue.name: RX_FIFO_1
enumeratedValue.description: Timeout is controlled by Rx FIFO 1.

enumeratedValue.name: BELOW_ERR_LVL
enumeratedValue.description: Below error level. The receive counter is below the error passive level of 128.

enumeratedValue.name: AT_ERR_LVL
enumeratedValue.description: At error level. The receive counter has reached the error passive level of 128.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: No error: No error has occurred since the LEC bits has been reset by successful reception or transmission.

enumeratedValue.name: STUFF_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: Stuff error: More than 5 equal bits in a sequence have occurred in a part of a received message where not allowed.

enumeratedValue.name: FORM_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: Form error: A fixed format part of a received frame has the wrong format.

enumeratedValue.name: ACK_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: AckError: The message transmitted by the MCAN was not acknowledged by another node.

enumeratedValue.name: BIT1_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: Bit1Error: During the transmission of a message (with the exception of the arbitration field), the device wanted to send a recessive level (bit of logical value 1), but the monitored bus value was dominant.

enumeratedValue.name: BIT0_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: Bit0Error: During the transmission of a message (or acknowledge bit, or active error flag, or overload flag), the device wanted to send a dominant level (data or identifier bit logical value 0), but the monitored bus value was recessive. During Bus_Off recovery this status is set each time a sequence of 11 recessive bits has been monitored. This enables the CPU to monitor the processing of the Bus_Off recovery sequence (indicating the bus is not stuck at dominant or continuously disturbed).

enumeratedValue.name: CRC_ERROR
enumeratedValue.description: CRCError: The CRC check sum of a received message was incorrect. The CRC of an incoming message does not match with the CRC calculated from the received data.

enumeratedValue.name: NOCHANGE
enumeratedValue.description: NoChange: Any read access to the protocol status register re-initializes the LEC bits to 0x7. When the LEC equals the value 0x7, no CAN bus event was detected since the last CPU read access to the protocol status register.

enumeratedValue.name: SYNCHRONIZING
enumeratedValue.description: Synchronizing - node is synchronizing on CAN communication.

enumeratedValue.name: IDLE
enumeratedValue.description: Idle - node is neither receiver nor transmitter.

enumeratedValue.name: RX
enumeratedValue.description: Receiver - node is operating as receiver.

enumeratedValue.name: TX
enumeratedValue.description: Transmitter - node is operating as transmitter.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: The MCAN is in Error_Active state. It normally takes part in bus communication and sends an active error flag when an error has been detected.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: The MCAN is in the Error_Passive state.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Both error counters are below the Error_Warning limit of 96.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: At least one of error counter has reached the Error_Warning limit of 96.

register.name: ABORT0
register.description: Channel Abort control for all DMA channels

cluster.name: CHANNEL[%s]
cluster.description: Array of registers: CFG, CTLSTAT, XFERCFG

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Hardware triggering not used for channel.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_LOW_FALLING
enumeratedValue.description: Active low - falling edge. Hardware trigger is active low or falling edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

enumeratedValue.name: ACTIVE_HIGH_RISING
enumeratedValue.description: Active high - rising edge. Hardware trigger is active high or rising edge triggered, based on TRIGTYPE.

enumeratedValue.name: EDGE
enumeratedValue.description: Edge. Hardware trigger is edge triggered. Transfers will be initiated and completed, as specified for a single trigger.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. Destination burst wrapping is not enabled for this DMA channel.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. Destination burst wrapping is enabled for this DMA channel.

field.name: CHPRIORITY
field.description: Priority of channel when multiple DMA requests are pending.

register.name: CTLSTAT
register.description: Control and status register for DMA channel

field.name: VALIDPENDING
field.description: Valid pending flag for this channel.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_TRIGGERED
enumeratedValue.description: Not triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is not set. DMA operations will not be carried out.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIGGERED
enumeratedValue.description: Triggered. The trigger for this DMA channel is set. DMA operations will be carried out.

register.name: XFERCFG
register.description: Transfer configuration register for DMA channel

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. The channels' control structure should not be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled. The channels' control structure should be reloaded when the current descriptor is exhausted.

field.name: SETINTA
field.description: Set Interrupt flag A for channel.

enumeratedValue.name: SET
enumeratedValue.description: Set. The INTA flag for this channel will be set when the current descriptor is exhausted.

field.name: SETINTB
field.description: Set Interrupt flag B for channel.

enumeratedValue.name: SET

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: DBLPWM is not split. PWMA and PWMB each have double pulses.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: DBLPWM is split to PWMA and PWMB.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enable fractional cycle length for the PWM period.

field.name: SPLIT
field.description: Split the DBLPWM signal to PWMA and PWMB

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: DBLPWM is not split. PWMA and PWMB each have double pulses.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: DBLPWM is split to PWMA and PWMB.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.description: Disable fractional cycle length for the PWM period.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enable fractional cycle length for the PWM period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to" method. This means that PWM edges are only produced when the counter is equal to one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period will maintain this state until a match with VAL3 clears the output in the following period.

enumeratedValue.name: EQUAL_TO_OR_GREATER_THAN
enumeratedValue.description: The VAL* registers and the PWM counter are compared using an "equal to or greater than" method. This means that PWM edges are produced when the counter is equal to or greater than one of the VAL* register values. This implies that a PWMA output that is high at the end of a period could go low at the start of the next period if the starting counter value is greater than (but not necessarily equal to) the new VAL3 value.

enumeratedValue.name: NORMAL
enumeratedValue.description: Normal mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFPINx]. If neither FHALF nor FFULL is set then the fault condition cannot be cleared. The PWM outputs disabled by this fault input will not be re-enabled until the actual FAULTx input signal de-asserts since the fault input will combinationally disable the PWM outputs (as programmed in DISMAPn).

enumeratedValue.name: SAFE
enumeratedValue.description: Safe mode. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear and FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FHLAF nor FFULL is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: MANUAL
enumeratedValue.description: Manual fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are not enabled until FSTS[FFLAGx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared. This is further controlled by FCTRL[FSAFE].

enumeratedValue.name: AUTOMATIC
enumeratedValue.description: Automatic fault clearing. PWM outputs disabled by this fault are enabled when FSTS[FFPINx] is clear at the start of a half cycle or full cycle depending on the states of FSTS[FHALF] and FSTS[FFULL] without regard to the state of FSTS[FFLAGx]. If neither FFULL nor FHALF is set, then the fault condition cannot be cleared.

enumeratedValue.name: LOGIC_0
enumeratedValue.description: A logic 0 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.

enumeratedValue.name: LOGIC_1
enumeratedValue.description: A logic 1 on the fault input indicates a fault condition.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_FLAG
enumeratedValue.description: No fault on the FAULTx pin.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM_OUTPUTS_NOT_REENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: PWM outputs are not re-enabled at the start of a full cycle

enumeratedValue.name: PWM_OUTPUTS_REENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: PWM outputs are re-enabled at the start of a full cycle

enumeratedValue.name: PWM_OUTPUTS_NOT_REENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: PWM outputs are not re-enabled at the start of a half cycle.

enumeratedValue.name: PWM_OUTPUTS_REENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: PWM outputs are re-enabled at the start of a half cycle (as defined by VAL0).

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Fault input glitch stretching is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Input fault signals will be stretched to at least 2 IPBus clock cycles.

enumeratedValue.name: BYPASS
enumeratedValue.description: Bypass the quadrature decoder. A positive transition of the PHASEA input generates a count signal. The PHASEB input and the REV bit control the counter direction. If the value of CTRL[REV] and PHASEB is same, then count is up. If the value of CTRL[REV] and PHASEB is different, then count is down.

field.name: SWIP
field.description: Software-Triggered Initialization of Position Counters UPOS and LPOS

enumeratedValue.name: INIT
enumeratedValue.description: Initialize position counter (using upper and lower initialization registers, UINIT and LINIT)

field.name: HNE
field.description: Use Negative Edge of HOME Input

enumeratedValue.name: POS
enumeratedValue.description: Use positive-going edge-to-trigger initialization of position counters UPOS and LPOS

enumeratedValue.name: NEG
enumeratedValue.description: Use negative-going edge-to-trigger initialization of position counters UPOS and LPOS

field.name: HIP
field.description: Enable HOME to Initialize Position Counters UPOS and LPOS

enumeratedValue.name: HOME
enumeratedValue.description: HOME signal initializes the position counter

enumeratedValue.name: NOTRANS
enumeratedValue.description: No transition on the HOME signal has occurred

enumeratedValue.name: TRANSI
enumeratedValue.description: A transition on the HOME signal has occurred

field.name: FILT_PRSC
field.description: prescaler divide IPbus clock to FILT clk

enumeratedValue.name: POSITIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Generates a positive quadrature decoder signal

enumeratedValue.name: NEGATIVE
enumeratedValue.description: Generates a negative quadrature decoder signal

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Disable updates of hold registers on the rising edge of TRIGGER input signal

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLED
enumeratedValue.description: Enable updates of hold registers on the rising edge of TRIGGER input signal

enumeratedValue.name: NOACTION
enumeratedValue.description: No action for POSD, REV, UPOS and LPOS registers on rising edge of TRIGGER

enumeratedValue.name: CLEAR
enumeratedValue.description: Clear POSD, REV, UPOS and LPOS registers on rising edge of TRIGGER

enumeratedValue.name: DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Last count was in the down direction

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Last count was in the up direction

enumeratedValue.name: INDEX
enumeratedValue.description: Use INDEX pulse to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)

enumeratedValue.name: COUNT
enumeratedValue.description: Use modulus counting roll-over/under to increment/decrement revolution counter (REV)

enumeratedValue.name: COMPARE
enumeratedValue.description: POSMATCH pulses when a match occurs between the position counters (POS) and the corresponding compare value (COMP )

enumeratedValue.name: READ
enumeratedValue.description: POSMATCH pulses when the UPOS, LPOS, REV, or POSD registers are read

field.name: SABIE
field.description: Simultaneous PHASEA and PHASEB Change Interrupt Enable

field.name: SABIRQ
field.description: Simultaneous PHASEA and PHASEB Change Interrupt Request

enumeratedValue.name: NOSIMUL
enumeratedValue.description: No simultaneous change of PHASEA and PHASEB has occurred

enumeratedValue.name: SIMUL
enumeratedValue.description: A simultaneous change of PHASEA and PHASEB has occurred

enumeratedValue.name: NOTUSED
enumeratedValue.description: Period measurement functions are not used. POSD is loaded to POSDH and then cleared whenever POSD, UPOS, LPOS, or REV is read.

enumeratedValue.name: USED
enumeratedValue.description: Period measurement functions are used. POSD is loaded to POSDH and then cleared only when POSD is read.

field.name: INTID
field.description: Interrupt ID of the interrupt to trigger, in the range 0-479.

register.name: AIRCR
register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register

field.name: VECTCLRACTIVE
field.description: Reserved for Debug use. This bit reads as 0. When writing to the register you must write 0 to this bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SYSRESETREQ
field.description: System reset request. This bit allows software or a debugger to request a system reset. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW if SYSRESETREQS is 0. When SYSRESETREQS is set to 1, from Non-secure state this bit acts as RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: Do not request a system reset.

field.name: SYSRESETREQS
field.description: System reset request, Secure state only. The value of this bit defines whether the SYSRESETREQ bit is functional for Non-secure use. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure State and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is available to both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is only available to Secure state.

field.name: PRIGROUP
field.description: Interrupt priority grouping field. This field determines the split of group priority from subpriority. This bit is banked between Security states

field.name: BFHFNMINS
field.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI Non-secure enable. The value of this bit defines whether BusFault and NMI exceptions are Non-secure, and whether exceptions target the Non-secure HardFault exception. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure-state and RO from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI are Secure.

enumeratedValue.name: NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault and NMI are Non-secure and exceptions can target Non-secure HardFault.

field.name: PRIS
field.description: Prioritize Secure exceptions. The value of this bit defines whether Secure exception priority boosting is enabled. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure state and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SAME_PRIORITY
enumeratedValue.description: Priority ranges of Secure and Non-secure exceptions are identical

field.name: ENDIANNESS
field.description: Data endianness bit. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: VECTKEY
field.description: Register key: Reads as 0xFA05. On writes, write 0x5FA to VECTKEY, otherwise the write is ignored. This Field is not banked between Security states.

register.name: SCR
register.description: The SCR controls features of entry to and exit from low-power state.

field.name: SLEEPONEXIT
field.description: Indicates sleep-on-exit when returning from Handler mode to Thread mode. Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR

field.name: SLEEPDEEP
field.description: Controls whether the processor uses sleep or deep sleep as its low-power mode. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SLEEPDEEPS
field.description: Controls whether the SLEEPDEEP bit is only accessible from the Secure state. This bit in only accessible from the Secure state, and behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Nonsecure state. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit is accessible from both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Non-secure state.

field.name: SEVONPEND
field.description: Send Event on Pending bit. When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE. The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wakeup the processor, disabled interrupts are excluded.

enumeratedValue.name: INCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wakeup the processor

register.description: The MPU Type Register indicates how many regions the MPU support. Software can use it to determine if the processor implements an MPU.

field.name: SEPARATE
field.description: Indicates support for separate instruction and data address maps. RAZ. Armv8-M only supports a unified MPU

field.name: DREGION
field.description: Number of regions supported by the MPU. If this field reads-as-zero the processor does not implement an MPU.

field.name: HFNMIENA
field.description: Enables the operation of MPU during HardFault and NMI handlers

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: MPU is disabled during HardFault and NMI handlers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: The MPU is enabled during HardFault and NMI handlers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Disables the default memory map. Any instruction or data access that does not access a defined region faults.

enumeratedValue.name: DISABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enables the default memory map as a background region for privileged accesses.

field.name: REGION
field.description: Indicates the memory region accessed by MPU_RBAR and MPU_RASR.

field.name: XN
field.description: The XN bit is an Execute Never bit, that indicates whether the processor can execute instructions from the region.

enumeratedValue.name: EXECUTE
enumeratedValue.description: Execution is only permitted if read permitted.

field.name: AP
field.description: The AP[2:0] bits indicate the access and privilege properties of the region.

field.name: SH
field.description: For Normal memory regions, the S bit indicates whether the region is shareable. For Strongly-ordered and Device memory, the S bit is ignored.

field.name: BASE
field.description: Contains bits[31:5] of the lower inclusive limit of the selected MPU memory region. This value is zero extended to provide the base address to be checked against.

field.name: ATTRINDX
field.description: Attribute index. Associates a set of attributes in the MPU_MAIR0 and MPU_MAIR1 fields.

field.name: LIMIT
field.description: Limit address. Contains bits[31:5] of the upper inclusive limit of the selected MPU memory region. This value is postfixed with 0x1F to provide the limit address to be checked against.

field.name: XN
field.description: The XN bit is an Execute Never bit, that indicates whether the processor can execute instructions from the region.

field.name: ATTR0
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 0.

field.name: ATTR1
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 1.

field.name: ATTR2
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 2.

field.name: ATTR3
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 3.

field.name: ATTR4
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 4.

field.name: ATTR5
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 5.

field.name: ATTR6
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 6.

field.name: ATTR7
field.description: Memory attribute encoding for MPU regions with an AttrIndex of 7.

field.name: ENABLE
field.description: Enable. Enables the SAU. This bit is RAZ/WI when the Security Extension is implemented without an SAU region.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURED_MEMORY
enumeratedValue.description: Memory is marked as Secure and is not Non-secure callable.

field.name: SREGION
field.description: SAU regions. The number of implemented SAU regions.

register.name: RNR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Number Register

register.name: RBAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Base Address Register

field.name: BADDR
field.description: Base address. Holds bits[31:5] of the base address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the base address are defined as 0x00.

register.name: RLAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Limit Address Register

field.name: NSC
field.description: Non-secure callable. Controls whether Non-secure state is permitted to execute an SG instruction from this region.

field.name: LADDR
field.description: Limit address. Holds bits[31:5] of the limit address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the limit address are defined as 0x1F.

field.name: ADDRESS
field.description: When the SFARVALID bit of the SFSR is set to 1, this field holds the address of an access that caused an SAU violation.
